zones.html:
NW Fishing

September 10, 2026

Best bets for weekend fishing:

  • Nehalem Bay has fall Chinook in the bay and tidewater. Fishing has been fair and consistent the past couple weeks with multiple fish being caught daily. The Bag limit is one wild adult Chinook per day and five for the season (July 1 to Nov 30) as part of the overall daily bag limit. A few hatchery coho have been caught in the bay as well.
  • Wild coho fisheries is open in Nehalem, Tillamook, and Nestucca Bays, the season runs until October 28 (Open Wednesdays, Saturdays, and Sundays only). As part of your 2 adult salmon/steelhead per day, only 1 can be a wild adult coho. No more than 3 wild adult coho per season in any one basin (Nehalem, Tillamook, and Nestucca). No more than 5 wild adult coho salmon may be harvested per year in the Northwest and Southwest Zones. See the regulation updates online at Fall coastal salmon management for more details. It is early in the season and coho numbers will be low in the bays but a few are showing up.
  • Nestucca Bay and Tillamook Bay are both starting to produce Fall Chinook, it's early but there are some around and being caught in both estuaries.
  • Cape Meares Lake and Town Lake were stocked with trophy trout last week. These are 2-3 pound trout that are fun to catch!
  • Warm water fisheries for bass and sunfish are active and provide some good opportunity for weekend fishing. Cape Meares Lake, Coffenbury Lake, Cullaby Lake, and Vernonia pond all have decent populations of warm water species available to catch. Lake Lytle has a good largemouth bass population, but it is very weedy. The bass populations in Cape Meares and Coffenbury are healthy with decent numbers and size of fish. The population is down in Town Lake.
  • Summer steelhead fishing on the Siletz River has been slow, but last week's rain should get some fish moving again. Multiple batches of summer steelhead were recycled to the lower river for additional angler opportunity in May and June. Recycled steelhead have a colored tag at the base of the dorsal fin. Anglers are asked to please report tagged steelhead caught in the Siletz River to caleb.w.yann@odfw.oregon.gov with the date, tag color, and general location where fish were caught to monitor recapture and harvest rates in the basin. Additional summer steelhead were also recycled to Olalla Reservoir to provide angler opportunities.
  • The Siuslaw, Alsea, Siletz and Yaquina rivers are starting to produce some fall Chinook lower in the systems.
  • Sea-run and resident cutthroat can be found in many Mid Coast streams currently open to angling. Anglers are reminded to be aware of daily bag limits, bait restrictions and additional angling closures.
  • Warmwater fisheries can be a great option this time of year. Siltcoos and Tahkenitch lakes can be great places to target largemouth bass, yellow perch, and bluegill. Largemouth bass are doing well at both locations.
  • Siletz River HWY 229 remains closed at approximately milepost 14 due to a large land slide covering the road.

Trout stocking

September:

Lost Lake, Town Lake, Coffenbury Lake, Cape Meares Lake, Sunset Lake (N Coast Range)

Check out the trout stocking schedule.

Trout stocking maps

Check out the ODFW fishing and trout stocking maps to find nearby fishing locations, driving directions and descriptions of amenities.

Announcements

Three Rivers from the mouth to the hatchery deadline is closed to angling July 16 to September 30.

Trask River 200 feet above and 900 feet below Gold Creek at Trask Hatchery (which includes the "hatchery hole") is closed to angling July 16 to October 15.

New for 2026: Tillamook Bay and River upstream of the Hwy 131 bridge is closed to all sturgeon angling (including catch and release).

Trask Hatchery has some damage to their access road, the hatchery is still open to the public, but as a result anglers and visitors alike will need to park up top and walk down.

The Trask is closed to angling from the marker at the Dam Hole (MP 7 on Trask River Road) up to Blue Ridge Creek September 1 – November 30.

Many coastal basins opened for fall Chinook on August 1. For regulation updates visit Fall Coastal Salmon Management for more information.

Big Creek from the RR trestle to the hatchery deadline is closed to angling until Oct. 15.

Sign up for the latest information on boater access

Marine Board's Opportunities and Access Report incorporates information from federal and state agencies, local facility operators and fellow boaters to provide up-to-date information so boaters can decide where to recreate and what to expect this season. Subscribe to receive email updates.

Updates by waterbody

ALSEA RIVER: Cutthroat trout, Chinook salmon

Fall Chinook opened August 1. Anglers have reported catching a fair number of Chinook in the bay over the past week. The wild Chinook bag limit is two per day/ten for the season from August 1 to December 31, as part of the overall daily bag limit. Wild Chinook jacks may be retained as per the permanent regulations (up to 5/day). See the regulation updates online at Fall coastal salmon management for more details.

Sea-run and resident cutthroat trout are available throughout the Alsea River. Check your regulations before you head out for bait or stream restrictions. Last updated 9/9/26.

KILCHIS RIVER: Cutthroat trout

There are cutthroat trout throughout Kilchis and plenty of public access off Kilchis Forest Road. Sea-run cutthroat have been in tidewater and are dispersing upriver now.

Fall Chinook season opened August 1 and there may be a few fish moving into tidewater, but numbers will be low until a little later in the run. The wild Chinook bag limit is one adult per day/five for the season from August 1 to November 30, as part of the overall daily bag limit (in aggregate with Tillamook Bay, Miami R, Kilchis R, Wilson R, Trask R, and Tillamook R). Wild Chinook jacks may be retained as per permanent regulations (up to 5/day). See the regulation updates online at Fall coastal salmon management for more details. Last updated 9/8/26.

NECANICUM RIVER: Cutthroat trout

There are cutthroat trout throughout the Necanicum River fishery. Sea-run cutthroat have been in tidewater and are in the river now as well. Concentrate on deep pools with cover and use stealthy tactics for the best odds of success.

Technically Fall Chinook fishing opens in the Necanicum on August 1, and there may be a few moving into tidewater, but the numbers will be low until later in the fall, thus far very few fish have been caught. The wild Chinook bag limit is one adult per day/five for the season from August 1 to November 30, as part of the overall daily bag limit. Wild Chinook jacks may be retained as per the permanent regulations (up to 5/day). See the regulation updates online at Fall coastal salmon management for more details.

The Highway 101 boat ramp south of Seaside will be closed to vehicle access until next fall to reduce dumping and illegal camping. A combination lock will be put back on the gate for angler access next fall usually around mid-October. Walk in access is still permitted through the summer. Last updated 9/8/26.

NEHALEM RIVER & NORTH FORK NEHALEM: Chinook, coho, Cutthroat trout

The Nehalem gets a run of "summer" Chinook salmon (an early component of the Fall run) and those fish have been in the bay and tidewater and some may have moved into the river. Fishing has slowed a bit the past week but is still fair and consistent with multiple fish being caught daily. August is generally the peak month for the early run of Chinook. At the same time the more traditionally timed fall Chinook are starting to show up. This is mostly a bay fishery with trolling spinners being a popular method lower in the bay and bobber fishing in the upper tidewater. Fish are dispersed from the jaws to the upper tidewater.. The wild Chinook bag limit is one adult per day/five for the season from July 1 to November 30, as part of the overall daily bag limit. Wild Chinook jacks may be retained as per the permanent regulations (up to 5/day). See the regulation updates online at Fall coastal salmon management for more details.

There have been a few hatchery coho caught down near the jaws, but it's probably still a little early for the Nehalem hatchery coho headed for the North Fork. The wild coho fishery will be opening in Nehalem this week. The season is September 9 to October 28 (Open Wednesdays, Saturdays, and Sundays only). As part of your 2 adult salmon/steelhead per day, only 1 can be a wild adult coho. No more than 3 wild adult coho per season from the Nehalem basin. No more than 5 wild adult coho salmon may be harvested per year in the Northwest and Southwest Zones. See the regulation updates online at Fall coastal salmon management for more details.

There are cutthroat trout throughout the Nehalem basin and no shortage of places to fish for them. Sea-run cutthroat are dispersed throughout the fishery. Fishing has been good for them recently. Remember to check for bait restrictions before fishing.

The Nehalem River above the Hwy 26 bridge at Elsie is closed to all angling September 1 – November 30. Last updated 9/8/26.

NESTUCCA RIVER & LITTLE NESTUCCA RIVER: Summer steelhead, cutthroat trout, Chinook

Fall Chinook are starting to show up in Nestucca Bay with some fish being caught the past couple of weeks. The wild Chinook bag limit is one adult per day/two for the season from August 1 to November 30, as part of the overall daily bag limit. Wild Chinook jacks may be retained as per the permanent regulations (up to 5/day). See the regulation updates online at Fall coastal salmon management for more details.

The wild coho fishery will be opening in the Nestucca this week. The season is September 9 to October 28 (Open Wednesdays, Saturdays, and Sundays only). As part of your 2 adult salmon/steelhead per day, only 1 can be a wild adult coho. No more than 3 wild adult coho per season from the Nestucca basin. No more than 5 wild adult coho salmon may be harvested per year in the Northwest and Southwest Zones. See the regulation updates online at Fall coastal salmon management for more details. It is still a little early for coho but there should be a few starting to show up.

The Nestucca also gets a hatchery summer steelhead run. Many anglers switch to salmon fishing in the fall but September and October can be a great time to target summer steelhead. The cooler water temperatures and fall rains can get these fish more active and willing to bite. Even though they have been in the river for a few months they aren't going to spawn until winter so many of them are still good table fair. There are fish present throughout the fishery (up to Elk Creek), and Cedar Creek Hatchery has been recycling summer steelhead to increase angler opportunity. Some rain this week may get them more active and improve fishing. Lures, beads, and jigs are all effective techniques.

There are cutthroat trout throughout the Nestucca basin. Sea-run cutthroat are dispersed throughout the fishery. Fishing should be fair to good. Last updated 9/8/26.

River levels and predictions for the Nestucca are available here.

SALMON RIVER: Cutthroat trout, Chinook salmon

Fall Chinook opened August 1. Some Chinook are being caught, but many fish will not move in for a couple more weeks. The wild Chinook bag limit is two per day/ten for the season from August 1 to December 31, as part of the overall daily bag limit. Wild Chinook jacks may be retained as per the permanent regulations (up to 5/day). See the regulation updates online at Fall coastal salmon management for more details.

Resident and sea-run cutthroat trout are available in the Salmon River. Be sure to check your regulations before you head out for bait or stream restrictions. Last updated 9/9/26.

SILETZ RIVER: Summer steelhead, Chinook salmon, cutthroat trout

Summer steelhead are dispersed throughout the Siletz River, but fishing has been slow. Most anglers are targeting the gorge upstream of Moonshine Park. The bank access in the upper gorge offers a unique and often remote fishing experience for anglers looking to get away from crowds. Multiple batches of summer steelhead were recycled to the lower river for additional angler opportunity in May and June. Recycled steelhead will have a colored tag at the base of the dorsal fin. Anglers are asked to please report tagged steelhead caught in the Siletz River to caleb.w.yann@odfw.oregon.gov with the date, tag color, and general location fish were caught. Thank you to all the anglers who have been reporting tagged steelhead.

Fall Chinook opened August 1. Anglers have reported catching a few Chinook in the bay and tidewater. More fish should be moving in over the next few weeks. The wild Chinook bag limit is two per day/ten for the season from August 1 to December 31, as part of the overall daily bag limit. Wild Chinook jacks may be retained as per the permanent regulations (up to 5/day). See the regulation updates online at Fall coastal salmon management for more details.

Resident and sea-run cutthroat trout are available in the Siletz River. Be sure to check your regulations before you head out for bait or stream restrictions. As a reminder, fishing is closed on the Siletz River and tributaries upstream of Siletz Falls

A landslide on HWY 229 has resulted in a road closure at approximately milepost 14.5. HWY 229 will be closed for the unforeseeable future until crews are able to safely remove the debris from the roadway.

As a general reminder for Anglers: Help to protect boating opportunities by maximizing distance from bank anglers and other boats. Safely row or motor around anglers and other boats and avoid motoring nearshore and in shallow areas. Last updated 9/9/26.

SIUSLAW RIVER: Cutthroat trout, Chinook salmon, rockfish, surf perch, crabbing

Fall Chinook opened August 1. Reports indicate a few Chinook are being caught in the lower river between the mouth and Cushman. The wild Chinook bag limit is one per day/five for the season from August 1 to December 31, as part of the overall daily bag limit. Wild Chinook jacks may be retained as per the permanent regulations (up to 5/day). See regulation updates online at Fall Coastal Salmon Management for more details.

Resident and sea-run cutthroat trout are available in the Siuslaw River. Be sure to check your regulations before you head out for bait or stream restrictions.

Jetties can be a great place to target rockfish and surf perch during the summer. For more information on surf perch, crabbing, rockfish and lingcod, refer to the Marine Recreation Report. Last updated 9/9/26.

THREE RIVERS: Cutthroat trout

Three Rivers from the mouth to the hatchery deadline is closed to angling until September 30. The best opportunity upstream of the hatchery weir is for cutthroat trout as hatchery Chinook and steelhead are stopped at Cedar Creek hatchery. Resident cutthroat are present throughout the upper portion of the stream. Last updated 9/8/26.

TILLAMOOK BAY: Chinook, coho, marine bottom fish.

Fall Chinook fishing opened in the Tillamook basin (Tillamook Bay, Miami R, Kilchis R, Wilson R, Trask R, and Tillamook R) on August 1. There's been some Chinook caught in the bay the past couple weeks; both in the lower and upper bay. The wild Chinook bag limit is one adult per day/five for the season from August 1 to November 30, as part of the overall daily bag limit. Wild Chinook jacks may be retained as per the permanent regulations (up to 5/day). See the regulation updates online at Fall coastal salmon management for more details.

The wild coho fishery will be opening in Tillamook this week. The season is September 9 to October 28 (Open Wednesdays, Saturdays, and Sundays only). As part of your 2 adult salmon/steelhead per day, only 1 can be a wild adult coho. No more than 3 wild adult coho per season from the Tillamook basin. No more than 5 wild adult coho salmon may be harvested per year in the Northwest and Southwest Zones. See the regulation updates online at Fall coastal salmon management for more details. Tillamook Bay also gets a run of hatchery coho headed for the Trask River. It is still a little early for coho but there should be a few starting to show up.

There are still rockfish and kelp greenling available off the Tillamook Bay jetties (the North jetty provides the only bank angling this spring as the South jetty is still undergoing repairs/construction). Ling cod fishing tends to be slower this time of year but there should still be a few around. Concentrate on slack tides for the best chance of success. Sea-run cutthroat have dispersed into the rivers but there should still be a few in the tidewater. Last updated 9/8/26.

TRASK RIVER: Chinook, cutthroat trout, coho

Chinook fishing is slow on the Trask. What fall Chinook are around are mostly in the bay and tidewater although a few have been caught in the lower river. The wild Chinook bag limit is one adult per day/five for the season from August 1 to November 30, as part of the overall daily bag limit (in aggregate with Tillamook Bay, Miami R, Kilchis R, Wilson R, Trask R, and Tillamook R). Wild Chinook jacks may be retained as per the permanent regulations (up to 5/day). See the regulation updates online at Fall coastal salmon management for more details.

The Trask River gets a return of hatchery coho that should start coming back this month, but for now they will mostly be in the estuary. There is no retention of wild coho allowed upstream of the Hwy 101 bridge.

The Trask is closed to angling from the marker at the Dam Hole (MP 7 on Trask River Road) up to Blue Ridge Creek September 1 – November 30. The section of the Trask River 200 ft above and 900 ft below Gold Creek at Trask Hatchery (which includes the "hatchery hole") is closed to angling until October 15.

Trout fishing is open and there are cutthroat trout (including sea-runs) throughout the fishery, which includes the North, South, and East forks (no bait allowed in the forks between May 22-Aug 31). Fishing is fair to good.

Trask hatchery has some damage to the access road so anglers and visitors will need to park up top and walk down if passing through to upstream areas. Last updated 9/8/26.

WILSON RIVER: Summer steelhead, cutthroat trout.

Summer steelhead are in the Wilson River. Many anglers switch to salmon fishing in the fall but September and October can be a great time to target summer steelhead. The cooler water temperatures and fall rains can get these fish more active and willing to bite. Even though they have been in the river for a few months they aren't going to spawn until winter so many of them are still good table fair. Fish are throughout the fishery (up to the South Fork) and the upper river seems to have the best numbers. There is plenty of public access off Highway 6. Lures, beads, and jigs are all proven techniques.

There are cutthroat trout (including sea-runs) throughout the Wilson River.

Fall Chinook season opened August 1 and there may be some moving into tidewater but probably still won't be much upstream. The wild Chinook bag limit is one adult per day/five for the season from August 1 to November 30, as part of the overall daily bag limit (in aggregate with Tillamook Bay, Miami R, Kilchis R, Wilson R, Trask R, and Tillamook R). Wild Chinook jacks may be retained as per the permanent regulations (up to 5/day). See the regulation updates online at Fall coastal salmon management for more details. Last updated 9/8/26.

Wilson River levels and predictions are available here.

YAQUINA RIVER: Cutthroat trout, Chinook salmon, rockfish, surf perch, crabbing

Fall Chinook opened August 1. Angling pressure has been light, but there are a few fall Chinook being caught. The wild Chinook bag limit is two per day/ten for the season from August 1 to December 31, as part of the overall daily bag limit. Wild Chinook jacks may be retained as per the permanent regulations (up to 5/day). See the regulation updates online at Fall coastal salmon management for more details.

Resident and sea-run cutthroat trout are available in the Yaquina River. Be sure to check your regulations before you head out for bait or stream restrictions.

Jetties can be a great place to target rockfish and surf perch during the summer. For information on marine species such as surf perch, rockfish and lingcod, refer to the Marine Recreation Report. Last updated 9/9/26.

zones.html:
SW Fishing

September 10, 2026

Best bets for weekend fishing:

  • Some of the more popular spots to fish for red-tailed surfperch are along beaches like Horsefall Beach and Whiskey Run. Anglers have the best success fishing with sand shrimp weighted gear on the bottom although power grubs can also work.
  • Try warmwater fishing for bass at Ben Irving, Howard Prairie and Hyatt Reservoirs.
  • Cooper Creek Reservoir looks nice and clear. Go earlier in the morning or fish deeper for success.
  • This is a good time of year to look for cutthroat in the Chetco River estuary. The estuary has very little bank access. Please be mindful of out-migrating salmon and steelhead smolt. If you catch these young salmonids, consider switching to barbless hooks and/or moving to a new location.
  • Hemlock and Lake of the Woods are accessible, and people are catching good numbers of trout.

Trout stocking

Stocking schedules in SW Zone have been impacted by lower-than-normal water levels, higher temperatures and lack of accessibility for liberation trucks.

Please see individual waterbodies for updates or check the Trout stocking schedule.

September:

Fish Lake

Trout stocking maps

Check out the ODFW fishing and trout stocking maps to find nearby fishing locations, driving directions and descriptions of amenities.

Sign up for the latest information on boater access

Marine Board's Opportunities and Access Report incorporates information from federal and state agencies, local facility operators and fellow boaters to provide up-to-date information so boaters can decide where to recreate and what to expect this season. Subscribe to receive email updates.

Updates by waterbody

AGATE LAKE: Bass, carp, black crappie, yellow perch, brown bullhead, trout

Agate Lake is 15 percent full and likely to start dropping in the coming weeks. The Agate Lake Boat Launch is open. There should still be rainbow trout available. Fishing crank baits and poppers can be a lot of fun for bass as the water starts to warm up through next week. Anglers are encouraged to harvest any carp or catfish caught at the reservoir and chicken liver is a good bait to target them. Last updated 8/26/26.

APPLEGATE RESERVOIR: Trout, landlocked spring chinook, largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, black crappie, bluegill

The lake level is 1,909.48ft and the surface temperature at Applegate is 70F. Check up-to-date reservoir levels here, or call the Army Corps of Engineers at (800) 472-2434 for lake level and temperature information.

Holdover trout should be evenly distributed throughout the reservoir until the air temperatures start to climb. Bank fishing or trolling should be good. Bass fishing along the vegetation and structure along the banks should also start to get good with the forecast of warmer weather in the next week.

There is a longstanding health advisory for consumption of resident species due to elevated levels of mercury. See Oregon Health Authority consumption guidelines or the sportfishing regulations for more information. Last updated 9/9/26.

APPLEGATE RIVER below Applegate Dam: Hatchery rainbow trout

As of May 22, anglers may fish for hatchery rainbow trout in the mainstem. Wild rainbow and cutthroat trout must be released. Please be mindful of out-migrating salmon and steelhead smolt. If you catch these young salmonids, consider switching to barbless hooks and/or moving to a new location. No new updates. Last Updated 7/30/26.

BEN IRVING RESERVOIR: Rainbow trout, bass, bluegill, yellow perch, crappie

Ben Irving was stocked with rainbow trout in April and again in the middle of May. Trout fishing should be slow with the warmer weather, so try fishing deeper to find cooler water. Crappie and bass are some of the best bets for now. Last update 9/9/26.

BOLAN LAKE: Rainbow trout, brook trout

The Bolan Lake Campground and the day use areas are open after renovations. Check USFS Bolan Lake Campground website for more information. The lake was stocked with 800 legal-size rainbow trout on May 21. Spinners have been very productive based on recent reports. There are good bank access and a small unimproved boat ramp available. No new updates. Last updated 7/21/26.

CHETCO RIVER: Cutthroat trout

Summer is a good time to beat the heat and head higher up in the river and search for trout. Anglers that don't have a boat can find good numbers of cutthroat in all the bigger tributaries of the Chetco and upper mainstem. Please be mindful of out-migrating salmon and steelhead smolt. If you catch these young salmonids, consider switching to barbless hooks and/or moving to a new location. No new updates. Last updated 7/8/26.

COOPER CREEK RESERVOIR: Rainbow trout, bass, bluegill, yellow perch, crappie

The water looks nice and clear. Try going earlier in the morning or deeper for trout. Bait may be a better choice. some notably large largemouth bass have been spotted lately. The reservoir was last stocked with trout in mid-May with legal rainbows. Bass angling has been good.

The West boat ramp is now open to the public.

Common carp have been illegally introduced into the reservoir. If one should catch a carp, please take a photo, get the size, and location fish were caught and send to evan.leonetti@odfw.oregon.gov or call the Roseburg office at (541) 440-3353. Do not release the fish back into the water. Last updated 9/9/26.

COOS RIVER BASIN: Bottomfish, trout, surfperch, steelhead, salmon, trout

Sneaker waves warrant caution when fishing along the jetties, however, rockfish can be caught around the jetties in the lower Coos Bay estuary, but you may need to move around to several spots to find actively biting fish. Best fishing is typically near slack tides with good fishing one day and fair fishing the next. A jig fished with a twister tail trailer is always a good option to catch bottom fish or sand shrimp.

For the general marine fish regulations, please visit the sport bottomfish seasons page.

The salmon bite is typically best a couple hours before and through the high slack tide. Regulations have been updated to 2 fish per day in the Bay and river (hatchery or wild). A third fish may be retained but must be hatchery. The run of Coos River basin produced Chinook returning to the bay have started entering from the ocean. Chinook fishing has been slow-fair depending on the day. The wild coho season will open in Coos Bay from 9/19/26 to 10/18/26 with a daily bag limit of 1 per day and 3 for the year. Last updated 09/8/26

Choose a day when the surf is not at a dangerous level, and it is possible to catch a few striped perch around the jetties. Some of the more popular spots to fish for red-tailed surfperch are along beaches like Horsefall Beach and Whiskey Run. Anglers have the best success fishing with sand shrimp weighted gear on the bottom although power grubs can also work. Last updated 9/8/26.

ODFW stocking of coastal lakes in the district (Saunders, Bradley, Butterfield, Empire Lakes, Powers) has been curtailed until fall. Conditions are too warm for trout at this point. Trout season is open in streams. Last updated 9/08/26.

THERE MAY BE A TEMPORARY DOCK MOORED TO THE CHANDLER BRIDGE ON THE COOS RIVER TO ALLOW FOR BRIDGE MAINTENANCE. BOATERS IN THIS REACH OF RIVER NEED TO BE AWARE OF THIS BOATING RISK.

COQUILLE RIVER BASIN: Trout, striped bass, steelhead, smallmouth bass, salmon

Striped bass fishing in the lower Coquille is usually at its best in June; however, fish can still be picked up with persistence in August and September. Fish using nightcrawlers or 1/3 of an anchovy/herring bait on the bottom along current lines in 8-12ft of water. Use of a sliding line through a three-way swivel or swivel stopper with drop lead is popular. Topwater large minnow style gear can work as well, mornings, in the evening and moonlit nights. Last updated 9/8/26.

Smallmouth bass are fully active with the warmer weather. Fishing should pick back up with recent rains and slightly lower river temps. Topwater gear can work well as temperatures move back down to the 60's. When fishing slows try bait on the bottom or artificial grubs/worms worked slowly. There is no limit for smallmouth bass, which are destructive to salmon fry production.

Steelhead have finished their spawning run for 2026, and fishing is over for the season. There has been some confusion about use of bait in the Coquille basin during the steelhead season due to the language in the S.W. section Regulations Exceptions. Bait is allowed in all mainstem forks of the Coquille basin for steelhead. The plan at this point is to adjust the language in the regulations for the 2027 regulations manual. Last updated 9/8/26.

The wild coho fishery will open 9/19/26 to 10/13/26 from Hwy 101 upstream to Sturdivant Park. Bag limit will be 1 fish per day, 3 for the year. Hatchery Chinook only may be retained from 9/19/26 to 10/18/26 from Hwy 101 to Sturdivant Park.

For any questions on Salmon Fishing in the Coos or Coquille please call the Charleston office at (541) 888-5515 *dial zero in the options menu.

ODFW has curtailed stocking of coastal lakes in the district (Saunders, Bradley, Butterfield, Empire Lakes, Powers Pond) until waters cool in the fall. There continues to be a few trout available to be caught. Trout fishing has been slow in those locations, largemouth bass, perch, are also in the above noted lakes. Trout fishing is open in all streams within the Coos and Coquille basins as of May 22. No new updates. Last updated 9/8/26.

DIAMOND LAKE: Trout

All boat ramps are open. The main ramp cleaning station is under repair and will not be open until a further date. Angling has been good with several limits being reported and lots of brown and tiger trout being released.

Diamond Lake has been stocked with tiger and brown trout. These fish were introduced to help control illegally introduced tui chub. These trout are catch-and-release only and need to be released immediately and unharmed if caught. Follow these catch-and-release tips for reducing fish mortality. Last updated 9/9/26.

ELK RIVER: Cutthroat trout

Cutthroat are scattered throughout the watershed this time of year. Spinners or flies work well. Please be mindful of out-migrating salmon and steelhead smolt. If you catch these young salmonids, consider switching to barbless hooks and/or moving to a new location. No new reports. Last updated 7/8/26.

EMIGRANT LAKE: Largemouth and smallmouth bass, black crappie, bluegill, brown bullhead, catfish, rainbow trout

Emigrant Lake is 5 percent full. The most current elevations for Emigrant Reservoir and other Rogue Basin reservoirs can be found on the Bureau of Reclamation's website, here. The North ramp is open for paddle craft to carry to the water. The West Boat Ramp is closed.

Largemouth bass fishing is starting to get good around the drop-offs in the still portions of the reservoir. Try targeting smallmouth bass near the head of the reservoir where there is some current from inflow.

There is a longstanding health advisory for consumption of resident warmwater species in Emigrant for high levels of mercury. Consult the sportfishing regulations or the Oregon Health Authority for more information on consumption guidelines. Last updated 9/9/26.

EXPO POND: Rainbow trout, largemouth bass, bluegill, black crappie

Fishing for largemouth bass and panfish should start to pick up as days warm up, but anglers can catch nice Largemouth Bass year-round here. Try fishing Senko's or brush hogs on a light jig and let them sink naturally with a little bit of slack in the line.

Expo Pond is the pond at the Jackson County Fairgrounds located directly adjacent to the access road at Gate 5, at Southern Oregon RV Park.

There are Chinese mystery snails in the most northern pond. They are highly invasive and were illegally dumped here. Please do not move these creatures and drain and dry any personal watercraft before using them in another waterbody. Last updated 8/4/26.

FISH LAKE: Rainbow trout, brook trout, spring Chinook

The lake level is 17 percent full. The USFS public boat ramp is closed effective immediately due to low water levels. Fish Lake Resort has confirmed that parking and launching is available at the resort for $6 fee. Please contact the resort directly for more details. Early season trolling for trout is usually very good this time of year.

Anglers are encouraged to report catches of tiger trout or send other fishing reports to Rogue Fish District Staff (541) 826-8774. No new reports. Last updated 9/9/26.

FLORAS LAKE: Rainbow trout, cutthroat, bass

Although the lake is not known for bass, anglers can find a few hanging out in some of the shallower parts of the lake this time of year. Anglers will still need to pay attention to the wind. Mornings are typically calmer than afternoons. The lake has very little bank angling. Boat anglers can launch at Boice Cope County Park. No new reports. Last updated 7/8/26.

GALESVILLE RESERVOIR: Rainbow trout, bass

The boat ramp is still accessible but may soon be inaccessible to larger boats. The reservoir is about 40 feet lower than summer full pool. The reservoir was last stocked in Mid-May. A lower reservoir can mean the fish are concentrated and easier to target. Angling effort is slow. Last updated 9/9/26.

GARRISON LAKE: Trout, bass

Anglers may want to focus their attention on bass as the water temperatures and vegetation are making trout fishing a little tough. Anglers should check weather conditions before heading out. The lake can be very windy. Conditions are typically calmer in the morning. No new reports. Last updated 7/8/26.

HEMLOCK LAKE & LAKE IN THE WOODS (Douglas County): Trout

Fishing is good at Hemlock and slow at Lake in the woods. Both lakes were stocked in mid-June with legal rainbows. Hemlock was stocked with 750 larger rainbows last week. Last updated 9/9/26.

HOWARD PRAIRIE: Trout, bass

Howard Prairie is 52 percent full. The reservoir has been stocked with plenty of legal-sized trout and the full reservoir last year should have promoted very good growth for hold-over trout. The Willow Point and Klum Landing Park boat ramps are both open. Grizzly Park campground and day use areas are open for paddle craft to carry to the water. Largemouth bass fishing will likely start to pick up in the next few weeks. Try fishing with senkos, wedding rings, brush hogs, or other rubber baits on a jig head and let them sink naturally along docks or structures. Reports of anglers having success catching their daily trout limit and some largemouth bass in the process. Remember to remove all vegetation from gear, boots and boats before leaving Howard Prairie. Last updated 9/9/26.

HYATT LAKE: Trout, bass, brown bullhead, black crappie

Hyatt is 34 percent full. Hyatt has a lot of legal-sized trout in it, so fishing should be good. Fishing power bait a couple feet off the bottom near the dam is typically a good early season strategy for trout if you are bank fishing. Holdover trout should be good size this year. The Cascade boat ramp is now closed. The Mountain View Ramp is reported to be open but low reservoir levels may make launching difficult. Please launch at your own risk, aquatic vegetation has been fowling props close to the ramp. Gates at the boat ramps may be closed before 7am and after 8pm, check with the BLM camp host for details. If you have a boat, it can be worth casting lures in the shallow section on the north end of the reservoir while the water is still somewhat up and the water is still relatively cool. Largemouth bass fishing could start getting good as temperatures start to warm up. Rubber baits on a jig head are quite effective near the submerged trees. Last updated 8/31/26.

Reports of blue green algae bloom are on the rise. Please check the Oregon Health Authority website for updated information regarding advisories. Oregon Health Authority: Current Cyanobacteria Advisories: Cyanobacteria Blooms: State of Oregon

Remember to remove all vegetation from gear, boots, and boats before leaving Hyatt.

ILLINOIS RIVER: Hatchery rainbow trout

Beginning May 22, anglers may fish for hatchery rainbow trout in the mainstem. Wild rainbow and cutthroat trout must be released. Please be mindful of out-migrating salmon and steelhead smolts. If you catch these young salmonids, consider switching to barbless hooks and/or moving to a new location. No new updates. Last updated 7/30/26.

LAKE MARIE: Rainbow trout, yellow perch

This is a good lake to use scented bait. Stocking has been completed for the season. Recent reports indicate that fishing has been slow. Last updated 9/9/26.

LAKE SELMAC (Selmac Lake): Trout, largemouth bass, bluegill, crappie

Lake Selmac has been stocked with legal-sized rainbow trout a couple of times this year. This lake is an outstanding largemouth bass fishery, and the bluegill and crappie fishing can be fun, as well. Boat anglers, please do your part to remove as much vegetation as possible before leaving the ramp, as well as drain and dry vessels before boating in another waterbody. Please help stop the spread of Oregon's aquatic hitchhikers! No new updates. Last updated 7/30/26.

LEMOLO RESERVOIR: Brown trout, rainbow trout, kokanee

The lake was stocked in mid-June with 2,000 larger rainbows. Fishing for rainbow trout is good. The reservoir was stocked in Mid-May with rainbow trout and again last week with 1250 larger rainbows. For other information call the Lemolo Lake Resort at (541) 643-0750. Kokanee has a separate harvest limit of 10 per day, with no size limit. Last updated 9/9/26.

LITTLE HYATT LAKE: Trout, largemouth bass

Little Hyatt Res was stocked with 1,200 legal-sized rainbow trout in April, and anglers report good catches. Small rooster tails and blue-fox spinners seem to be working. No new updates. Last updated 7/30/26.

LOON LAKE: Warmwater species, trout

The BLM boat ramp is open until September 30. The lake was stocked in the middle of April, and again in Mid-May with legal rainbow trout. The Loon Lake Lodge ramp is open April through October 31. This ramp is private and has limited parking. It may be closed if it is full. You may want to call the lodge at (541) 599-2244 before heading out. Fishing should be good for trout and bass. Last updated 9/9/26.

LOST CREEK RESERVOIR: Rainbow trout, landlocked spring chinook, bass

The lake level is 1,790.44ft and the water surface temperature at Lost Creek is 66F. In addition to trolling, Lost Creek also offers good bank fishing access, and fishing on both sides of the lake near the dam can be very effective using PowerBait. Trolling wedding rings with a worm has been a proven method. Last updated 9/9/26.

Anglers can click here to get the latest reservoir details or by calling the US Army Corps Lost Creek Lake and Applegate Reservoir projects information line at (800) 472-2434.

MEDCO POND: Rainbow trout, largemouth bass, bluegill, black crappie

Medco Pond is a private pond, and access can be revoked at any time. A load of legal-size rainbows is anticipated to be stocked this week. Largemouth bass, bluegill, and crappie fishing are almost always a good bet here and a great way for young anglers to catch fish. Bank anglers should stay away from the east portion of the lake, again due to private property, and stay on the roadside of the gate with any vehicles (even if the gate is open). No new reports. Last updated 6/17/26. To help keep access open, please pick up any trash you may see.

PLAT I RESERVOIR: Trout, bass

Angling is slow for rainbow trout. Fish will be spread out now that the reservoir is at full pool. The reservoir was stocked in the middle of March with Rainbow trout. Last updated 9/9/26.

ROGUE RIVER

Rogue River, lower: Chinook, summer steelhead, half-pounder steelhead, surf perch

Good numbers of chinook are still being picked up in the bay and fishing will stay good through early October. Salmon are also starting to move up the river is pretty good numbers. Fishing in the river will still be a little tough until water temperatures drop a bit more. Anglers fishing early in the morning will find the best water temperatures and less boat traffic.

Half pounder steelhead are spread throughout the lower river. There are a few adult summer steelhead around, but the return is down this year. Last updated 8/25/26.

Rogue River, middle: Steelhead, Chinook

The middle Rogue is low this time of year. Please use proper catch-and-release techniques on fish that will not be harvested, such as keeping fish in the water as much as possible and releasing them quickly. No new reports. Last updated 7/30/26.

Current flow, temp and turbidity conditions for the Rogue can be found at the USGS stream gauges here, or checking the City of Grants Pass water page's river data here.

Rogue River, upper: Steelhead, Chinook

The release from Lost Creek Reservoir is around 1,450cfs and 54F. Click here for current flow at the Ray Gold gage. For up-to-date river levels, check all the USGS Rogue gauges here.

Cole Rivers Hatchery returns as of 9/2/26: New summer steelhead 7, season total 341. New spring Chinook 220, season total 16737. Folks are still catching a few hatchery and wild winter steelhead, and side-drifting larger beads seems to be the most productive. There are a few spring Chinook being caught, and angling pressure is starting to increase. If you don't intend to harvest a fish, please use proper catch-and-release techniques, such as keeping fish in the water as much as possible and releasing wild fish immediately. Last updated 9/9/26.

Rogue River, above Lost Creek Reservoir: Trout

Rogue River above Lost Creek Lake is anticipated to be stocked with 2,500 legal sized fish this week. Fly fishing can start to become quite good as hatches are starting to come out. Brown trout can also be caught in and around the North Fork Reservoir in Prospect. Bass crank baits or leech patterns fished near logs or structure can coax them to bite. Anglers are encouraged to harvest brook trout regardless of size. No new reports. Last updated 7/21/26.

Sixes River: Cutthroat

If winds are light, the estuary can be a good place to target cutthroat. Anglers can also find cutthroat scattered throughout the river, but access is very limited. Please be mindful of out-migrating salmon and steelhead smolt. If you catch these young salmonids, consider switching to barbless hooks and/or moving to a new location. No new reports. Last updated 7/8/26.

SMITH RIVER, Umpqua: Striped bass, trout, smallmouth bass, Chinook

Please be aware Smith River below Sisters Creek and North Fork Smith below Bridge 10 are open for catch-and-release only for trout. Above these locations it is open for retention. Smith River will close to all angling above Spencer Creek under permanent regulations beginning September 16 through November 30.

Smallmouth bass and striped bass are being caught in the tidewater sections. Angling for bass has been good. There are no harvest limits on any bass in the Smith River. There is also good access for angling since the Smith River Road follows the mainstem most of the time. Last updated 9/9/26.

SPALDING POND: Trout

Spalding pond was stocked in April. This is a nice quiet, high elevation pond west of Grants Pass. No new updates. Last updated 7/30/26.

TENMILE LAKES/TENMILE CREEK: Trout, largemouth bass, yellow perch, coho salmon

Largemouth bass in Tenmile Lakes can be active during mornings/evenings and can be caught on crankbaits, jigs, and finesse lures like drop shots. Look to find bass along submerged logs and deeper weed line edges. Fishing should be fair to good depending on the day.

Fish for yellow perch along the edge of the weed lines near the bottom and submerged structures. Fish the bottom with either a worm or a jig/jigging spoon tipped with a worm.

Steelhead fishing is over in the Tenmile Basin for the year as fish have matured and migrated to spawning areas and the adult hatchery trapping locations. Coho salmon do not enter the lake until November.

ODFW stocking of Tenmile and other lakes (Saunders, Bradley, Butterfield, Empire Lakes, Powers Pond) has been curtailed until fall. However, some trout are still present. Trout fishing has been slow in those locations. Trout fishing in the lakes is open year-round. Trout anglers can have success trolling in deeper water using wedding rings tipped with a nightcrawler. Last updated 9/8/26.

UMPQUA HIKE-IN LAKES AND FOREBAYS: Trout

Most of the lakes are accessible. No reports of angling conditions. Check with USFS for current trail and road conditions. Check out ODFW's trout stocking map for lakes stocked in the Southwest. Make sure to check the latest closures for wildfire in the South Umpqua. Last updated 9/9/26.

UMPQUA RIVER, *MAINSTEM: Fall Chinook, bass

Fall Chinook regulations Start July 1 through November 30. Anglers are finding a few Chinook and fin-clipped Coho near Reedsport. Bass fishing is good. A few good reports of some large striped bass have been reported. Last updated 9/9/26.

UMPQUA RIVER, NORTH: Trout

Returns of summer steelhead have fallen below the level where ODFW needed to take action to protect these fish. Following the framework developed in 2022, ODFW closed the North Umpqua to steelhead fishing beginning August 10 and continuing through November 30.

The North Umpqua will remain open for trout fishing in areas where allowed. Anglers are encouraged to use appropriate catch-and-release techniques due to the higher water temperatures currently in the basin. Last updated 9/9/26.

UMPQUA RIVER, *SOUTH: Bass, trout

Smallmouth bass fishing is good. Trout fishing is catch-and-release only. The South will close to all angling starting September 16 through November 30.

*Douglas County Permanent Recreational Use Advisory: South Umpqua River and mainstem Umpqua River

The advisory covers the South Umpqua River from Canyonville downstream to the confluence with the mainstem Umpqua River, and the mainstem Umpqua River downstream past Elkton to Sawyers Rapids. Pools in the bedrock along the rivers edge are known to develop cyanobacteria blooms that can be harmful to pets and people. Signs have been posted at several access areas along the river. Last updated 9/2/26.

WILLOW LAKE: Rainbow trout, largemouth bass, black crappie, brown bullhead, yellow perch

Largemouth bass fishing should start to get good as the weather is forecasted to warm up a bit over the next week. Dead-dropping rubber baits on a jig near stumps or willows along the margins can be very effective for bass. Willow Lake is about 2993.14acft full. Full pool is about 8,500acft. To check the current lake level click here. The boat ramp is closed; paddle crafts can carry down. There are opportunities for bank angling available. Last updated 9/9/26.

For more information on camping and day use please visit Jackson County Parks or call (541) 774-8183.

WINCHUCK RIVER: Cutthroat

If winds are light, the estuary can be a good place to target cutthroat. Anglers interested in fishing the river can find good cutthroat fishing and bank access on the forest service property. Please be mindful of out-migrating salmon and steelhead smolt. If you catch these young salmonids, consider switching to barbless hooks and/or moving to a new location. Remember, no angling from a floating device on this river; bank angling or wading only. No new reports. Last updated 7/14/26.

zones.html:
Willamette Fishing

September 10, 2026

Best bets for weekend fishing:

  • Last week's rain gave several valley waterways a cooling refresh to kickstart fall fishing.
  • Two-rod validation has been extended through Dec. 31 upstream of Willamette Falls.
  • ODFW stocked Blue Lake, St. Louis Ponds, Adair Pond, and Bond Butte Pond in July with channel catfish. These fish, sourced from an approved facility, averaged approximately one pound each and are expected to provide excellent summertime fishing opportunities in these valley ponds.
  • Try warmwater fishing for smallmouth bass and yellow perch near underwater structures and drop-offs in Foster Reservoir.
  • Fishing for walleye and smallmouth bass on the Willamette River between Salem and Corvallis can be very fun and exciting.

Trout stocking

Drought conditions are impacting Oregon waterways. The Trout Stocking Schedule is subject to change. Check the field notes below or contact the local ODFW office for questions about a specific area.

September:

Alton Baker Canal, McKenzie River 2 (Above Leaburg Dam), Estacada Lake, Foster Res, North Fork Res, Faraday Lake, Small Fry Lake, Henry Hagg Lake, Canby Pond, Hill Creek Res, Salish Pond, W.

Check out the trout stocking schedule.

Trout stocking maps

Check out the ODFW fishing and trout stocking maps to find nearby fishing locations (including high mountain lakes), driving directions and descriptions of amenities.

Announcements

An invasive Chinese mitten crab was captured in the Willamette near Portland. Read the news release here.

It is important to correctly identify this species and report it to 1-866-INVADER or report it online via the Oregon Invasive Species reporting hotline form. Photographs can be submitted through the hotline, and people are encouraged to do so as crab identification can be difficult, and native crabs have been misidentified as invasive.

Dexter Pond road closure

No public access into the Dexter Ponds Hatchery at least through Summer 2026 due to construction. Please call the USACE Park Ranger Office (541) 942-5631 with questions.

Sign up for the latest information on boater access

Marine Board's Opportunities and Access Report incorporates information from federal and state agencies, local facility operators and fellow boaters to provide up-to-date information so boaters can decide where to recreate and what to expect this season. Subscribe to receive email updates.

Updates by waterbody

ALTON BAKER CANOE CANAL (ABCC): Trout

Will be stocked every week in August and September with 900 hatchery rainbow trout.

The canoe canal is open to fishing all year and is located within Alton Baker Park. A 4-acre pond at the midpoint of the canal is a good spot to fish in, and behind the old Kowloon Restaurant. The canal can be fished all along its two-mile length from Day Island Road in Eugene to Aspen Street in Springfield. Last updated 9/1/26.

BLUE RIVER: Trout

Last stocked in June with 600 hatchery rainbow trout. Blue River is located east of Eugene near the town of Blue River, north of Hwy. 126 and is open to year-round fishing. Last updated 9/1/26.

BLUE RIVER RESERVOIR: Trout, warmwater species

Last stocked in June with 1,000 hatchery rainbow trout. The USFS has hired a concessionaire company to maintain the boat ramps and parking areas, and they are charging $9 to park at the Saddle Dam or Lookout Campground/boat launch parking area. For details people can call the USFS McKenzie Ranger District (541) 822-3381. Blue River Reservoir is located east of Eugene near the town of Blue River, north of Hwy. 126 and is open to year-round fishing. Last updated 9/1/26.

BREITENBUSH RIVER: Trout

This river feeds into Detroit Reservoir and offers several campgrounds along its steep, narrow course. It was stocked for the last time in mid-August with 900 hatchery trout. Flies or other light tackle work best, but bait is allowed. Anglers are allowed to keep 5 trout per day. Last updated 8/25/26.

CARMEN RESERVOIR: Trout

Last stocked the week of July 13 with 600 hatchery rainbow trout. No limit on size or number of brook trout harvested in Carmen Reservoir.

The reservoir is accessed via USFS Road 750 off Hwy. 126, about two miles south of Clear Lake. It is open to fishing all year. Use of bait is allowed. Motored boats are prohibited on this reservoir.

After nine years of closure, Carmen-Smith recreation sites on the Upper McKenzie River reopened to the public on May 1, offering hikers, and day visitors access to newly renovated facilities.

Anyone with questions about visiting these recreation sites should inquire online at https://www.fs.usda.gov/r06/willamette/recreation or by contacting the McKenzie River Ranger Station at (541) 822-3381. Last updated 9/1/26.

CLACKAMAS RIVER: Summer steelhead, spring Chinook, trout

There are still occasional spring Chinook and summer steelhead being caught in the Clackamas River. Coho fishing should start to pick up in September in the lower Clackamas River.

To report poaching or other violations: Call *OSP or *677 (*OSP on keypad). You also can call (800) 452-7888 or email TIP@osp.oregon.gov between the hours of 8-5, Monday-Friday. Take photos if it is safe to do so.

USGS hydrological data readings from the Estacada gauge near Milo McIver State Park. Hydrologic data and river forecasts can also be accessed on the NOAA/National Weather Service NW River Forecast Center -- NW River Forecast Center. Last updated 8/26/26.

CLEAR LAKE: Trout

Stocked for the last time this season August 17 with 3,000 hatchery rainbow trout.

Clear Lake is accessed from Hwy. 126 approximately 70 miles east of Springfield. Linn County's Clear Lake Resort rents cabins and boats. Last updated 9/1/26.

COAST FORK WILLAMETTE RIVER: Chinook, summer steelhead, trout

Was last stocked the week of July 27 with 800 hatchery rainbow trout.

The river is open to fishing all year for trout, hatchery Chinook salmon, hatchery steelhead and wild steelhead over 24 inches.

Use of bait is allowed April 22 – Oct. 31 but beginning Nov. 1 anglers may only use lures and artificial flies. In addition to five hatchery trout, two wild trout may be kept daily. Last updated 9/1/26.

COTTAGE GROVE POND: See Row River Nature Park Pond

COTTAGE GROVE RESERVOIR: Trout, spotted bass, largemouth bass, crappie, yellow perch, bluegill

Last stocked in April, with 3,750 hatchery rainbow trout. Cottage Grove Reservoir is south of Cottage Grove and is open to fishing all year. Updated 9/1/26.

DETROIT RESERVOIR: Trout

The reservoir gets stocked with trout during the late spring and summer. As a reminder, anglers are allowed to keep up to five trout, with an additional ten kokanee. It was last stocked with 6,900 trophy trout.

Mongold State Park boat ramp is still available. All other boat ramps are no longer in the water. After Labor Day weekend, the crowds will thin out, but the fish are still biting. Pretty much any technique will catch fish, but it might take some experimenting to find out what is most effective on the day you're out there.

It's always a good idea to check the water levels at the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers website before using the boat ramps. For the latest information on water levels at Detroit Reservoir check with the Army Corps of Engineers' website for more information. Last updated 8/31/26.

DEXTER RESERVOIR: Trout, largemouth bass, smallmouth bass

Last stocked in April with 3,000 hatchery rainbow trout. Dexter Reservoir near Lowell is visible from Hwy 58. Boat and bank access is available through state and county parks. Parking and bank access are also available from the causeway near Lowell. Last updated 9/1/26.

DORENA RESERVOIR: Trout, largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, yellow perch, crappie, bluegill

Last stocked in April with 5,500 hatchery rainbow trout. Surface water temperatures are high so fishing deeper waters of the lake will be more productive for trout.

Dorena Reservoir is east of Cottage Grove on Row River Road and is open to fishing all year. Baker Bay Park (Lane County) is open seasonally from April – October. The park has a boat ramp, ADA restrooms, showers, picnic and camp spots. Last update 9/1/26.

FALL CREEK: Trout

Last stocked in June with 1,200 hatchery rainbow trout. Fall Creek is open all year for trout. Bait is allowed from April 22 through Oct. 31; however, beginning Nov. 1, anglers may only use lures and artificial flies. Five hatchery trout and an additional two wild trout may be harvested daily in the river.

Fishing for salmon upstream of Fall Creek Dam is prohibited. Below Fall Creek Dam the creek is open all year for hatchery Chinook, hatchery steelhead and wild steelhead greater than 24 inches. Last updated 9/1/26.

FALL CREEK RESERVOIR: Trout

Last stocked in April, with 3,750 hatchery rainbow trout.

Water elevation as of August 4 is at 810 ft and both North Shore (729 ft) and Winberry (803ft) boat ramps should be accessible. Cascara (815ft) boat ramp is not accessible. Last updated 9/1/26.

FARADAY LAKE: Trout

Faraday Lake is now closed while PGE updates its powerhouse at Rivermill Dam. For more information, visit PGE's Parks and Recreation webpage.

FERN RIDGE RESERVOIR: Largemouth bass, crappie, bluegill, brown bullhead

This 9,000-acre lake just 12 miles west of Eugene is the Willamette Basin's largest waterbody. Orchard Park, Richardson Park, and Perkins Peninsula boat ramps are all open. For information regarding the lake and available boat ramps, contact the Lane County Parks Department at (541) 682-2000.

Midsummer the fish become less active during the day, but fishing can still be good late in the evening or early in the morning. Look for crappie along the weedy edges on the south side of the reservoir. The south shore around Perkins Peninsula as well as along the face of the dam are good spots.

There is good bank access at several rest stops and campgrounds, and three seasonal boat ramps. No new updates. Last updated 8/6/26.

FOSTER RESERVOIR: Trout, bass, perch, catfish

Foster Lake is in great shape at the moment. This waterbody is stocked with trout in the spring as well as in early fall. Besides trout, look for smallmouth bass and yellow perch near underwater structure and drop-offs. Please remember that only adipose fin-clipped trout may be kept as part of the 5-trout bag limit, but there are no limits on size or number of bass. In the summer, early morning and late evening are usually when fish become most active.

Retention of warmwater fish species such as bluegill, pumpkinseed, catfish, crappie, and yellow perch is allowed -- no limit on size or number. Anglers report good success in the two arms of the reservoir, as well as the shoreline in between. Trout and yellow perch can be caught year-round.

The reservoir is full, and all boat ramps are available. This scenic 1,200-acre reservoir on the South Santiam River is located just 30 minutes from Interstate 5. There is good bank access at several rest stops and campgrounds, and three seasonal boat ramps. No new updates. Last updated 8/10/26.

FREEWAY LAKE, EAST: Trout, bass, bluegill, crappie

Fishing for warmwater gamefish such as bass, bluegill, crappie and catfish can be very good, especially early and late in the day in spring and summer. Look for them near downed wood and along the edges of weed.

This waterbody consists of three interconnected ponds and features some good size bass and crappie. The largest pond on the west side of the highway is only accessible by boat. A boat ramp is available at East Freeway Lake, and there is some bank access around East and Middle Freeway Lake. No new updates. Last updated 7/27/26.

GOLD LAKE: Brook trout, rainbow trout

The lake is open for fishing annually from May 22 to Oct. 31. For access inquiries call the USFS Willamette National Forest (541) 782-2283 for updates.

Gold lake has special fishing regulations in place that include no retention of rainbow trout, no limit on brook trout, fly-fishing only, with fly rod, no spinning rigs, only barbless hooks. Oregon State Marine Board passed a regulation in 2020 that allows ELECTRIC motors only on Gold Lake.

Gold Lake is a 100-acre lake located north of the Willamette Pass summit off Hwy. 58 approximately 23 miles southeast of Oakridge. Last updated 9/1/26.

GREEN PETER RESERVOIR: Trout, smallmouth bass

This large reservoir has two seasonal boat ramps. Due to drought conditions, water levels are lower than normal and dropping slowly. Both boat ramps are effectively out of the water and will remain until at least February 1 when the storage season begins. Last updated 8/31/26.

HARRIET LAKE: Trout

Lake Harriet is currently closed due to safety and access concerns related to nearby active wildfires. Please do not visit these locations. For more information, visit PGE's Parks and Recreation webpage.

Harriet Lake is a 23-acre reservoir on the Oak Grove Fork of the Clackamas River in the Mount Hood National Forest. Boat ramp is just past the campground.

HENRY HAGG LAKE: Rainbow trout, largemouth bass, crappie, smallmouth bass, yellow perch, bluegill, bullhead catfish

The best times of day to target bass are in the mornings and evenings. Try downsizing your gear a bit and fish with jigs that mimic crayfish holding near the lake bottom.

Cappie fishing near the dam can be productive this time of year with many small fish available and a few larger ones in the mix as well. Try casting 1-inch Gulp minnows (chartreuse) from the bank or boat for some good panfish action.

Hagg Lake is one of western Oregon's largest lakes and is a premier warmwater fishing destination. The lake is home to both the state record smallmouth bass and bullhead catfish.

Current reservoir levels can be found here. Maintained and operated by Washington County, the park features numerous picnic areas, two boat launching facilities, more than 15 miles of hiking trails, and observation decks for wildlife and bird watching. The lake and lake park are currently open, although users are encouraged to check the Hagg Lake Park website, as conditions can change. Last updated 9/8/26.

HILLS CREEK RESERVOIR: Trout, crappie, bass

Will be stocked for the last time this season the week of September 28 with 3,000 hatchery rainbow trout.

Don't forget that you can keep hatchery Chinook in the reservoir as mentioned below. Hills Creek Reservoir is located about four miles southeast of Oakridge and is open to year-round fishing. In addition to catchable-size trout, the reservoir is stocked with 60,000 adipose fin-clipped rainbow trout fingerlings annually and 100,000 adipose fin-clipped spring Chinook salmon fingerlings (when available) to provide a harvest fishery the following year. This makes a great early-spring fishery on large fish.

Trout and salmon must be adipose fin-clipped to be harvested. Large native trout are available for catch-and-release fishing. Packard Boat Ramp (USFS) generally remains accessible at all normal reservoir elevations although it is probable that the landing will not be available after early September this year because of a shortage of inflow. Last updated 9/1/26.

LEABURG LAKE: Trout

Will be stocked for the last time this season the week of August 24 with 1,000 hatchery rainbow trout. Leaburg Lake is open to fishing all year. Bait can be used from April 22 until Oct. 31, but beginning Nov. 1, anglers may only use lures and artificial flies. All wild trout must be released. Only hatchery fish may be kept. Last updated 9/1/26.

MCKENZIE RIVER below Leaburg Lake (R1): Trout, steelhead, Chinook

Was stocked for the last time this season in the week of September 1 with 2,000 hatchery rainbow trout.

April 22 to October 31 anglers can use bait in the mainstem McKenzie River. Beginning Nov. 1, anglers may only use lures and artificial flies. Fishing for summer steelhead remains open throughout the year. All non-adipose fin-clipped trout must be released unharmed. Check the 2026 Sport Fishing Regulations for bait restrictions in the segment you plan to fish.

The lower McKenzie River is open to retention of adipose fin-clipped salmon and steelhead and non-adipose fin-clipped steelhead greater than 24 inches long. A Columbia River Basin Endorsement is required for anglers targeting salmon and steelhead in the McKenzie. Last updated 9/1/26.

MCKENZIE RIVER above Leaburg Lake (R2): Trout, steelhead

Will be stocked the last time for the season the week of September 7 with 2,000 hatchery rainbow trout.

ODFW will be passing summer steelhead above Leaburg Dam this season (2026). All non-adipose fin-clipped trout must be released unharmed. Bait is allowed from Leaburg Dam to Forest Glen Boat Ramp April 22 until Oct. 31. Starting Nov. 1, anglers may only use lures and artificial flies. Last updated 9/1/26.

MIDDLE FORK WILLAMETTE RIVER: Trout, steelhead, Chinook

The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers refurbished the boat ramp on the south side of the Middle Fork Willamette just below Dexter Dam allowing drift boat and raft access.

A Columbia River Basin Endorsement is required for anglers targeting salmon and steelhead.

The Middle Fork Willamette above Lookout Point and Hills Creek reservoirs are open to fishing using lures and artificial flies. All wild trout must be released upstream of Lookout Point Reservoir. The Middle Fork Willamette River is not stocked with hatchery trout. Last updated 8/24/26.

NORTH FORK RESERVOIR: Trout

Opened for trout retention on May 22. North Fork Reservoir is a 350-acre reservoir of the Clackamas River behind North Fork Dam approximately 5.2 miles east of Estacada. This reservoir has two boat ramps, boat moorage, 50 campsites, picnic areas, boat rentals, grocery story, fueling station, and ADA-accessible fishing platforms. It is big and deep enough, and is fed by the upper Clackamas River, to stay cool longer into the summer than most of the other lakes and ponds. No new updates. Last updated 6/4/26.

For more information, visit PGE's Parks and Recreation webpage.

QUARTZVILLE CREEK: Trout

This river above Green Peter Reservoir gets stocked regularly from late spring through the summer. It was stocked for the last time in early August with 1,650 hatchery trout. Current flows are about 25cfs. Best conditions for fishing are below 300cfs. Light tackle including flies works best, but bait is allowed. The river above Green Peter Reservoir is open year-round.

Trout are active year-round, and anglers are allowed to keep up to five fish daily. . Last updated 9/9/26.

ROW RIVER NATURE PARK POND (formerly Cottage Grove Pond): Trout, bass, bluegill

Last stocked with 1,250 hatchery rainbow trout in April.

The fishing dock has been replaced, and the Cascade Family Flyfishers have removed aquatic vegetation and blackberries around the pond to improve access and angling success. The pond is open to year-round fishing and is accessible from the asphalt pathway behind the truck scales on Row River Rd. In addition to fishing, these ponds also offer many wildlife viewing opportunities. Last updated 9/1/26.

SALMON CREEK: Trout

Last stocked the week of July 27 with 800 hatchery rainbow trout.

Salmon Creek is open to fishing all year. Anglers may only use lures and artificial flies. Use of bait allowed Apr 22 - Oct 31. Trout are released at multiple locations upstream to Black Creek. Two wild trout per day, 8-inch minimum length, may be kept in addition to five hatchery trout. No new updates. Last updated 9/1/26.

SALT CREEK: Trout

Salt Creek and its tributaries are open to fishing all year; it is an unstocked tributary to the Middle Fork Willamette River east of Oakridge. Anglers may only use lures and artificial flies. Use of bait is only allowed from Apr 22 - Oct 31. Two wild trout may be kept per day, 8-inch minimum length. Last updated 9/1/26.

SANDY RIVER: Summer steelhead, spring Chinook

Anglers are finding success from the hatchery downstream, but summer steelhead can be found throughout the system.

Check conditions at individual parks on Metro's website. No new updates. Last updated 7/27/26.

SANTIAM RIVER (NORTH FORK): Steelhead, trout, Chinook, coho

River levels best for fishing are at or below 3,000cfs, and the river is currently running at 1,670cfs at the gage in Mehama. Fishing for chinook is now closed until mid-October. Fishing for steelhead remains open year-round. At this time only a few coho have migrated above Willamette Falls, however another strong run is expected this year, and numbers should increase markedly over the next few weeks. Spin cast with lures or swing large streamer flies through the pools.

There are several large, downed trees in the river creating some dangerous hazards for boaters in the lower river. For more information check out the Oregon State Marine Board website.

Fishing for hatchery steelhead is open year-round. Bait is allowed between April 22 and October 31. Last updated 9/9/26.

SANTIAM RIVER (NORTH FORK) above DETROIT: Trout

This river is open year-round to fishing, but ideal conditions usually begin after snowmelt recedes in late June and continues through early October. Currently, flows are around 315cfs. It was stocked for the last time in mid-August with about 2,000 hatchery trout scattered across several release locations. Dead drifting a nymph fly or slow retrieving a small spinner can sometimes coax larger trout to bite. Last updated 9/9/26.

SANTIAM RIVER (SOUTH FORK): Bass, trout, steelhead

Fishing is generally best when flows are below 3,000cfs. Flows are currently at around 1,520cfs at the gage in Waterloo. The 2026 Chinook run is complete, but it has been fairly strong. Most adults are above Waterloo and are concentrating between Pleasant Valley boat ramp and Wiley Creek. The Chinook fishery is now closed until Oct. 15. The summer steelhead run turned out better than average this year. About 9,400 steelhead adults have been counting at Willamette Falls so far with a few more trickling in through September. They can be found throughout the river basin, with most fish concentrated in the upper 8 miles below Foster Dam. Fishing for hatchery steelhead is open year-round. The use of bait is now allowed through the end of October. Last updated 9/9/26.

SMITH RESERVOIR: Trout

Last stocked the week of July 13 with 1,000 hatchery rainbow trout.

After nine years of closure, Carmen-Smith recreation sites on the Upper McKenzie River have reopened to the public as of May 1, allowing hikers and day visitors access to newly renovated facilities.

Anyone with questions about visiting these recreation sites should inquire online at https://www.fs.usda.gov/r06/willamette/recreation or by contacting the McKenzie River Ranger Station at (541) 822-3381. Last updated 9/1/26.

TIMOTHY LAKE: Trout

Closed for public safety. View the complete closure order and map as detailed by the Portland General Electric Parks and the Mt. Hood National Forest Alerts. Last updated 9/3/26.

TRAIL BRIDGE RESERVOIR: Trout

After nine years of closure, Carmen-Smith recreation sites on the Upper McKenzie River have reopened to the public as of May 1, offering campers, hikers, and day visitors access to newly renovated facilities. Campsites at Trail Bridge Campground will be available for booking now on Recreation.gov. The first reservable date was May 14. Anyone with questions about visiting these recreation sites should inquire online at https://www.fs.usda.gov/r06/willamette/recreation or by contacting the McKenzie River Ranger Station at (541) 822-3381.

ODFW has discontinued trout stocking in Trail Bridge Reservoir. Wild trout must be released. Only flies and lures may be used. Last updated 9/1/26.

TRILLIUM LAKE: Trout

Access is open, and the lake has been stocked with more than 6,000 rainbow trout. No new updates currently. No new updates. Last updated 7/21/26.

TURNER LAKE: Bass, panfish, some trout

This approximately 70-acre lake just north of Turner is open to public fishing along the southern half where the boat ramp is. Non-gasoline powered trolling motors only are allowed. It is an old borrow pit and features largemouth bass, panfish such as bluegill, and trout in the cooler months. Bass fishing can be excellent early in the morning or late in the evening when the larger fish approach the shore to feed. There's a boat ramp on the southwest corner of the lake. It was stocked a couple of times this spring with several thousand hatchery trout. Because the lake is deep, trout can survive year-round. As a reminder, only one trout over 20 inches is allowed as part of a five-fish per day bag limit. No new updates. Last updated 6/30/26.

WALTER WIRTH LAKE: Trout, bass, panfish

This urban lake usually gets stocked from about Thanksgiving through May. The rest of the year anglers can target bluegill and bass. As a reminder, only one trout out of a 5-fish bag limit may be longer than 20 inches.

Walter Wirth is a 20-acre lake located within the City of Salem's Cascades Gateway Park with good access all the way around. No new updates. Last updated 7/6/26.

WILLAMETTE RIVER: Steelhead, spring Chinook, coho salmon, bass, walleye, shad, catch-and-release sturgeon

There isn't much salmonid opportunity in the Willamette River in late August, but there will be coho abundance increasing in the system beginning in September. Late September and October are great times to target coho, especially above Willamette Falls. Willamette River is about 75 degrees now, so warmwater fishing is a good option for the rest of the summer. Consider fishing for bass, walleye, and other warmwater species that reside in the Willamette River and Multnomah Channel. The section from Buena Vista up to Peoria is especially good for Walleye.

As a reminder, per permanent regulations, sturgeon angling is prohibited from the Lake Oswego–Oak Grove Railroad Bridge upstream to Willamette Falls from May 1 through August 31.

See Willamette Catch Summaries for more details on spring chinook, steelhead and sturgeon here.

River conditions and fish counts:

Daily report Willamette River Portland-Temperature/Visibility

Link to: Willamette Falls Fish Counts

Link to: Willamette River Morrison Bridge Hydro Data

Link to NOAA-Willamette River Forecast (Salem)

The Willamette often gets overlooked because it is so close. But this river offers convenience, good access and variety.

The river is ideal for small boats such as canoes and kayaks, but there are enough public access points for bank anglers as well. Consult Oregon Parks and Recreation Department for specific locations.

The upstream section between Albany and Harrisburg is open year-round for trout fishing, which can be very good when flows are cooperating. The river is in very good shape right now and anglers report good catches of smallmouth bass between Salem and Albany. Look for deep slot pools and the tail-end of long riffles and the head of pools where the fish are likely stacked up in feeding lanes.

Smallmouth bass can be a lot of fun to catch and are plentiful between Salem and Corvallis during summer. Anglers also report the occasional walleye up to 20 inches. Trout prefer the cooler water temperatures upstream of Corvallis. From Salem downstream there are plenty of largemouth bass in the deeper, quieter sections. Trout can be kept in some sections, but not in others. Consult the regulation booklet for details.
